title: Homelessness payments to nonprofits per bed in the federal inventory
question: How much did the homelessness department pay nonprofits for each bed it reported to the federal government?
finding: Per bed of any kind (shelter, transitional, supportive, rapid rehousing, other permanent): $10,687 in 2019 and $21,096 in 2025 (+97%), as the money went from $158.9 million to $489.4 million (+208%) and the count from 14,864 to 23,200 (+56%). Per shelter, transitional or safe-haven bed: $46,682 in 2019 and $101,185 in 2025 (+117%), as the money went from $158.9 million to $489.4 million (+208%) and the count from 3,403 to 4,837 (+42%).
how: Money as above. Beds: year-round beds in the Housing Inventory Count that San Francisco files with the federal housing department each January. The first line divides by every bed in the inventory; the second repeats, for comparison, the shelter-only figure already shown under "Results against spending".
limits: Beds in the federal inventory include some the homelessness department does not pay for (veterans' and privately funded programmes), and nonprofit payments leave out rent paid directly to landlords and City-staffed sites. The January 2021 inventory was cut by pandemic distancing rules. The money is everything the department paid nonprofits that year, so this is the cost of the whole system set against one result, not the price of that result: most of the money keeps people housed, sheltered or in care who are not counted as a new result. A falling count can reflect harder cases or fewer openings rather than weaker work, and the pandemic distorted 2020 to 2022.
